# John Meredith

## Overview

- **Age:** Middle-aged  <sub>[v5 c2 P24](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0024)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v5 c2 P7](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0007)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v5 c35 P0](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0000)</sub>
- **Origin:** Maywater  <sub>[v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046)</sub>
- **Role:** Presbyterian Minister at Glen St. Mary  <sub>[v5 c2 P7](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0007), [v5 c2 P13](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0013)</sub>
- **Titles:** Reverend  <sub>[v5 c2 P7](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0007)</sub>; Mr.  <sub>[v5 c2 P7](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0007)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Jack  <sub>[v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Meredith is a tall, slender man with a pale, ivory-like complexion, dark hair falling over his high brow, and fine, clear-cut dark eyes. His features are described as handsome and comely, giving him a refined, scholarly, and gentlemanly appearance. In moments of distraction, he is known to wander about in unbrushed clothes, carpet slippers, and a faded dressing gown.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P6](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0006), [v5 c2 P14](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0014), [v5 c2 P26](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0026), [v5 c14 P4](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0004), [v5 c14 P28](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0028), [v5 c26 P11](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0011)_

## Personality

John Meredith is a deeply spiritual, scholarly, and idealistic man, but he is notoriously absent-minded and lacking in practical common sense. He is a dreamer who often gets lost in books or theological speculations, rendering him oblivious to his surroundings and his domestic affairs. Gentle, tender-hearted, and incapable of harshness, he loves his children deeply, though his detachment often leaves them to manage themselves. While generally shy and quiet, he possesses a rare eloquence in the pulpit and can be surprisingly firm and dignified when confronted.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P11](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0011), [v5 c2 P27](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0027), [v5 c4 P1](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0001), [v5 c4 P17](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0017), [v5 c14 P28](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0028), [v5 c14 P30](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0030), [v5 c26 P11](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0011)_

## History

After the death of his beloved wife Cecilia, John Meredith was left to raise their four young children alone. Upon accepting a call to the Presbyterian church in Glen St. Mary, he moved his family to the parish manse. Due to his intense absorption in theological studies and his dreamer's disposition, he neglected the practical oversight of his household and offspring, leaving them largely under the inadequate care of his aged, ailing relative, Aunt Martha. Although his powerful sermons won the admiration of his congregation, his children's wild pranks and untidy appearances caused frequent local gossip. When Mrs. Alec Davis rudely offered to adopt his daughter Una, Mr. Meredith was severely shaken into recognizing his shortcomings as a father. Determined to make amends and provide a proper mother for his children, he eventually realized his deep affection for Rosemary West. Despite a temporary setback due to an old vow made by Rosemary to her sister, the obstacles were cleared away—largely through the intervention of Una—and Mr. Meredith married Rosemary in a double wedding alongside Norman Douglas and Ellen West.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P7](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0007), [v5 c2 P11](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0011), [v5 c2 P25](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0025), [v5 c4 P1](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0001), [v5 c14 P16](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0016), [v5 c14 P28](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0028), [v5 c14 P29](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0029), [v5 c21 P1](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0001), [v5 c34 P38](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0038), [v5 c35 P0](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0000)_

## Background by volume

- Formerly lived and preached in Maywater before receiving the call to Glen St. Mary  <sub>[v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046)</sub>
- His first wife, Cecilia, died four years prior to his arrival in Glen St. Mary  <sub>[v5 c2 P25](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0025), [v5 c4 P1](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0001)</sub>
- Took in an elderly, semi-blind cousin, Aunt Martha, to avoid sending her to the poorhouse  <sub>[v5 c2 P25](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0025)</sub>
